subject: EU & APAC: Jurisdictional Cutover Playtest and Network Boundary Checklist
messages:
From: Paige Liu <paige.liu@cloudops.example.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: EU Procurement <procurement@euclient.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment playtest: jurisdictional cutover questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for agreeing to run the private-deploy cutover playtest for Eurolink Health next week. Before we lock the window, procurement asked me to confirm a couple of things so their legal & networking teams can sign off: 

- We need a short network boundary checklist confirming that no egress to non-EU/APAC regions will occur during the cutover. Can Redwood provide the ACLs and route table snapshots you intend to apply?
- For the warm-standby failover, what IP ranges will be announced and from which AZ/region so our peering team can pre-authorize filters?
- Any KMS/HSM key usage changes during cutover? Our compliance folks prefer a short note if keys will be rotated or rewrapped.

We'd like to schedule a 60-minute playtest window on Tue Apr 13 (UTC) but are flexible if your ops team prefers a different time.

Attachments: none in this message

Thanks,
Paige Liu
CloudOps Lead, AICorp
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Paige Liu <paige.liu@cloudops.example.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment playtest: jurisdictional cutover questions

Paige — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned and can provide the artifacts. High level responses below; attaching the working cutover runbook and the ACL matrix for your peering team to review.

1) Network boundary & ACLs
- We'll apply a temporary egress-only ACL that restricts outbound flows to EU (10.8.0.0/16) and APAC (10.20.0.0/16) peered ranges for the duration of the test. See attached network_acl_matrix.csv (tab "playtest-locked").

2) IP announcements and failover source
- Warm-standby announcement will originate from our APAC control cluster (apac-standby-1) with advertised ranges 198.51.100.0/24 (APAC) and 203.0.113.0/24 (EU secondary). Primary origin remains eu-control-2. We will provide LOAs for these ranges to Eurolink's peering team.

3) KMS/HSM usage
- No key rotations or rewrapping scheduled; we will use existing customer keys scoped to the Eurolink deployment. Any key-level admin ops will be performed prior to the playtest and communicated via the signoff doc.

Proposed plan: Tue Apr 13, 14:00–15:00 UTC for the playtest (60 min). Action items:
- Eurolink peering team to pre-approve the announced ranges in their edge filters (procurement in CC).
- Eurolink compliance to confirm KMS note is sufficient.
- Redwood to run the cutover runbook and capture route/ACL snapshots.

Attachments: [cutover_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF)], [network_acl_matrix.csv (CSV)]

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Paige Liu <paige.liu@cloudops.example.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment playtest: jurisdictional cutover questions

Adding a couple of operational checks from the networking side:

- BGP community tagging: we'll tag the standby announcements with community 65432:10 to make it visible in Eurolink's routing telemetry. Please confirm Eurolink will accept that tag.
- Healthcheck probes: during the cutover we'll switch probe source IPs to the APAC probe pool; ensure your firewall allows 198.51.100.128/26.
- SNAT behavior: note that some infra components do SNAT for telemetry — the runbook includes a short section (pg 8) where we temporarily disable SNAT for telemetry flows to guarantee no unexpected egress.

I've updated network_acl_matrix.csv (tab "ops-notes") with the healthcheck and community entries. Also included a minimal iptables diff in the attachment for on-prem proxy hosts.

Attachments: [network_acl_matrix.csv (CSV), iptables-proxy-diff.txt (TXT)]

-jw
From: Paige Liu <paige.liu@cloudops.example.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: EU Procurement <procurement@euclient.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment playtest: jurisdictional cutover questions

Thanks Mina & Jonas — this level of detail is great. Procurement confirms they have the LOA template and will attach it to the HubSpot deal once we confirm ranges. Compliance reviewed the KMS note and is OK as long as no rotations happen during the window.

Two small asks before we sign off:
- Can Redwood provide a one-page observable checklist (post-cutover) that includes the exact route snapshots and a short traffic sampling report showing no non-EU/APAC egress?
- If possible, please move the start time 30 minutes later (14:30–15:30 UTC) to align with our regional on-call.

If those two are OK we can consider this approved from our side and procurement will circulate the signoff doc.

Paige
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Paige Liu <paige.liu@cloudops.example.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment playtest: jurisdictional cutover questions

Paige — all good. Confirming final plan and deliverables below.

Playtest window: Tue Apr 13, 14:30–15:30 UTC (updated per Eurolink request).
Deliverables Redwood will produce (post-cutover within 2 business days):
- Route snapshots (BGP table dump) capturing announcement origin and community tags.
- ACL/iptables snapshots (before/during/after).
- One-page traffic sample report confirming zero egress to non-EU/APAC IP ranges.
- Signed playtest_signoff_form.docx (procurement template filled).

Operational notes:
- No KMS rotations during window. Keys remain bound to Eurolink tenancy.
- Jonas: standby will advertise 198.51.100.0/24; eu-control will remain primary origin. Marcus will push the ACLs at t-10 and snapshot at t+2.
- Soojin will collect telemetry samples and produce the one-pager.

Attachments: [playtest_signoff_form.docx (DOCX)]

Next steps (owners):
- Eurolink procurement: attach LOA & confirm filters (Paige)
- Redwood networking: LOA + ACLs (Jonas / Marcus)
- Redwood observability: sampling + report (Soojin)

If there are no objections, I'll mark this as the final signoff and circulate the DocuSign link after we get the LOA.

—Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
